Messages.Author: Scott Halvorson
Messages.Body:
I asked this question earlier, but I wasn't able to read newsgroups in
time to
see the reply to this question, so here goes again. If a minion in
combat has
a gun, and uses the maneuver on the gun to go to range, and then uses
the gun
for his strike, and the opposing minion plays Primal Instincts, does the
gun
minion get to choose another strike, or does he not get another strike,
because
he is forced to use the gun for his strike? Perhaps he can throw his
gun at the
opposing minion for 1R or 2R damage.... (-:

Scott Halvorson
halv...@cptc.wisc.edu

Oops. Overlooked the part of the explanation in the previous thread.
Primal Instincts cancels "this minion's" strike - not the opposing
minion's strike. If the guy with the .44 maneuvers with the .44 and
then plays Primal Instinct, he still has to strike with the .44.

Messages.Author: Xian
Messages.Body:
In article <75ockd$ci1$1...@nnrp1.dejanews.com>,
vte...@wizards.com (LSJ) wrote:
> In article <75o5a4$6gg$1...@nnrp1.dejanews.com>,

> Oops. Overlooked the part of the explanation in the previous thread.
> Primal Instincts cancels "this minion's" strike - not the opposing
> minion's strike. If the guy with the .44 maneuvers with the .44 and
> then plays Primal Instinct, he still has to strike with the .44.

So...to paraphrase (closely) Justin (?) from last time, "The opposing minion
is required to read the card again." Minion A maneuvers iwth the .44. Go to
strike phase. Minion A shoots with the .44. Minion B plays Primal
Instincts, which is *really* useless as the blocking minion (unless used for
the dodge...). Minion B has payed 1 blood to re-choose his strike which he
has not yet chosen. Use this card if you're the *acting* minion, not the
*blocking* minion.

Xian
